title: Dr. CBS on Trump's Black/Red Scare
content:
Dr. CBS on Trump's Black/Red Scare







Authors







Black Agenda Radio with Margaret Kimberley










bareditors




Fri, 07/31/2026 - 04:25













The U.S. Department of State released "Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism," which justifies the genocidal siege against that country while also attempting to criminalize leftist organizing. This document was preceded by the National Security Presidential Memorandum-7 (NSPM-7), which provides more rationales for state repression. What is the history of these scares and how do they impact Black people? 

Dr. Charisse Burden Stelly

 is the author of 

"Black Scare/ Red Scare: Theorizing Capitalist Racism in the United States,

" which was published in 2023.  She will also discuss her recently completed project, "This Is America," which appeared on Instagram.

Kshama Sawant

She is now running for Congress in Washington's 9th District as a socialist candidate, and the open "jungle" primary election for that race takes place on August 4th. She joins us from Seattle to discuss her campaign.

content:

Authors







Black Agenda Radio with Margaret Kimberley










bareditors




Fri, 07/24/2026 - 04:14













The Trump administration has accelerated its attacks on leftist organizations and individuals while also justifying its genocidal siege of Cuba with the release of the document "Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism." This follows Executive Order National Security Presidential Memorandum-7 (NSPM-7), which calls for state repression and the criminalization of leftist organizing. Ajamu Baraka, Black Agenda Report contributing editor and Director of the 

North-South Project for Peoples Centered Human Rights

, provides analysis on this newest iteration of state repression in the U.S.

title: Trump Administration Ends TPS for Haitians
content:
Trump Administration Ends TPS for Haitians







Authors







Black Agenda Radio with Margaret Kimberley










bareditors




Fri, 07/17/2026 - 04:07













On June 25, the Supreme Court of the United States ruled that Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haitians and Syrians would end. What does this ruling mean for the more than 350,000 Haitians living in the US under TPS? Brian Concannon is Executive Director of the 

Institute for Justice & Democracy in Haiti

, a US-based NGO that creates pathways to justice and accountability for human rights violations in Haiti. He joins us from Boston to discuss the impact of the Supreme Court decision.
